'''''Medicago littoralis''''' is an [[annual plant]] species of the genus ''[[Medicago]]''. Its native range encompasses the [[Mediterranean Basin]], from [[Macaronesia]] to the [[Caucasus]]; it has been introduced elsewhere. It is useful as a forage for livestock. As a [[leguminous]] plant, it is capable of adding nitrogen to soils, through its [[symbiotic]] relationship with the bacterium ''[[Sinorhizobium meliloti]]'', which enables [[nitrogen fixation]]. Common names include '''shore medick''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''water medick''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=MELI5|taxon=Medicago littoralis|access-date=28 January 2016}}</ref> '''coastal medick''', and '''strand medick'''.<ref name=powo/>

==Description==
{{expand section|date=January 2024|small=no}}
''Medicago littoralis'' is a prostrate or procumbent herb, occasionally with an ascending habit.<ref name=powo>{{cite web |title=''Medicago littoralis'' Rohde ex Loisel |publisher=Kew Science |website=Plants of the World Online |access-date=2 January 2024 |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:506264-1 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="pastures">{{citation |last1=Howie |first1=Jake |last2=Lloyd |first2=David |title=Factsheet – Strand medic |url=https://keys.lucidcentral.org/keys/v3/pastures/Html/Strand_medic.htm |publisher=Pastures Australia |id=Australian Wool Innovation (AWI), Grains Research and Development Corporation (GRDC), Meat and Livestock Australia (MLA), Rural Industries Research and Development Corporation (RIRDC), Dairy Australia |date=2009 |via=Lucid Keys Central |access-date=3 January 2024 |archive-date=16 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220816154955/https://keys.lucidcentral.org/keys/v3/pastures/Html/Strand_medic.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> 

==Distribution and habitat==
The species has been introduced to Belgium, the US states of [[Florida]] and [[New Jersey]], Great Britain, the Netherlands, and to parts of Australia.<ref name=powo/> It is [[Naturalisation (biology)|naturalised]] in [[South Australia]] and considered "alien" but non-invasive in [[Western Australia]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Medicago littoralis – Species Details |url=https://florida.plantatlas.usf.edu/plant.aspx?id=4384 |website=Atlas of Florida Plants}}</ref><ref>{{multiref|1={{cite encyclopaedia |title=Fact sheet for ''Medicago littoralis'' |publisher=The State Herbarium of South Australia: Government of South Australia |url=http://www.flora.sa.gov.au/cgi-bin/speciesfacts_display.cgi?genus=Medicago&species=littoralis |encyclopaedia=The Electronic Flora of South Australia}}|2={{cite encyclopaedia |title=''Medicago littoralis'' Loisel. Strand Medic |url=https://florabase.dbca.wa.gov.au/browse/profile/4075 |publisher=Western Australian Herbarium, Biodiversity and Conservation Science; Government of Western Australia |encyclopaedia=Florabase—the Western Australian Flora}} }}</ref>

==Agricultural uses==
{{expand section|date=January 2024}}
'Seraph',  is a specially bred variety of ''M. littoralis'', selected for its resistance to powdery mildew and tolerance of [[sulfonylurea]] herbicide residues.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Peck |first1=David |author2=South Australian Research and Development Institute |title=Strand Medic (''Medicago littoralis'') Variety: 'Seraph' |journal=Plant Varieties Journal |date=28 June 2021 |volume=34 |issue=1 |pages=297–299 |url=https://www.ipaustralia.gov.au/tools-and-research/professional-resources/ip-rights-journals/plant-varieties-journals |issn=1030-9748}} [https://www.ipaustralia.gov.au/tools-and-research/professional-resources/ip-rights-journals/~/-/media/Project/IPA/IPAustralia/PDF/PBR-Journals/Volume-34-Number-1.pdf (PDF direct download] – 5 MB)</ref>
